territory: Cross-cutting lens: scale to 2,000 users — findMany/take audit across all 594 src files, pagination audit (keyset vs offset), N+1 hunt, @@index coverage vs the ~20 hottest query shapes in prisma/schema.prisma, over-fetching in list views, O(n-users) fanout paths, per-pageview layout cost (auth/notifications/catchup-sweep/presence/mail-drain), and third-party quota math (Resend, Upstash, Turnstile, Sentry, PostHog, R2/Vercel image pipeline)

findings.title: Like has no postId-leading index: every feed page's like-counts and the 'Most liked' sort scan the entire Like table, and deleting a prolific author's account cascades through hundreds of full-table scans
findings.expected: Counting likes per post (WHERE postId = ?) and the FK cascade from Post deletion should be index lookups. Postgres does not auto-index FK columns; a child-side index on Like.postId is required.
findings.actual: Like's only index is `@@unique([userId, postId])` (schema.prisma:465), which leads with userId and cannot serve postId-only predicates. Every feed page (`_count: { select: { comments: {...}, likes: true } }`, feed/actions.ts:859), the letters index (letters/page.tsx:58), saved posts (feed/actions.ts:996), and the 'liked' sort (`orderBy: { likes: { _count: "desc" } }`, feed/actions.ts:893) all count likes per post. Prisma executes relation counts as a grouped aggregate/lateral count on Like WHERE postId — with no usable index that is a full scan of the Like table per request. Plausible 2,000-user row count: ~20k posts x ~10 likes = ~200k Like rows, rescanned on every feed/letters/saved page load; the offset-paged 'liked' sort additionally re-aggregates the whole table per page. Worse: `prisma.$transaction([report.deleteMany, user.delete])` in account-purge.ts:99 cascades User→Post→Like; Postgres runs the FK cascade per deleted Post row, each doing an unindexed lookup WHERE postId = <id> — an author with 500 posts triggers ~500 sequential full scans of a 200k-row table inside one transaction, which can run for minutes, hold a pgbouncer pooled connection, and fail the retention sweep's purge.
findings.evidence: schema.prisma Like model in full: `model Like { id String @id @default(cuid()); userId String; postId String; user User @relation(...); post Post @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade); @@unique([userId, postId]) }` — no other index. Feed include at feed/actions.ts:859: `_count: { select: { comments: { where: { isHidden: false, deletedAt: null } }, likes: true } }` runs on every loadPosts call (PAGE_SIZE 20, line 762). Sort at :891-894: `sortBy === "liked" ? { likes: { _count: "desc" } } : ...` with `skip: offset` (:900). A btree on (userId, postId) can only satisfy WHERE postId=? via a full index scan; the comments count by contrast has `@@index([postId, isHidden])` (schema:454), showing the pattern was applied to Comment but missed on Like.
findings.fixDirection: Add `@@index([postId])` to Like in schema.prisma via a dated idempotent file in prisma/migrations-manual/ (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS), run npx prisma generate, apply with scripts/dev/run-sql.mjs per the repo's schema-change protocol. While in there, add the sibling child-side FK indexes from the companion findings in one migration.
findings.gateOrTest: Extend the schema-assertion style of src/lib/security-regressions.test.mjs: a unit test that reads prisma/schema.prisma and fails if Like lacks a postId-leading @@index. Orchestrator can confirm live read-only with EXPLAIN on `SELECT "postId", COUNT(*) FROM "Like" WHERE "postId" IN ('x') GROUP BY 1` (Seq Scan today, Index Only Scan after).
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: EXPLAIN the aggregate above against the live DB, or time /feed with Prisma query logging on localhost. Code-argument is sufficient.

findings.title: Comment has no parentId index: opening any comment thread runs a full scan of the entire Comment table (the OR-on-parentId query cannot use the postId indexes)
findings.expected: Fetching the replies of a page of root comments should be an index lookup on parentId.
findings.actual: Comment's indexes are `@@index([postId, createdAt])` and `@@index([postId, isHidden])` only. loadComments' second query (feed/actions.ts:1147-1152) is `where: { OR: [ { id: { in: rootIds }, ...VISIBLE_COMMENT }, { parentId: { in: rootIds }, ...VISIBLE_COMMENT } ] }` — no postId filter at all, so the parentId branch has no usable index and the whole query degrades to a scan of the full Comment table (plausible ~100k rows at 2,000 users: 20k posts x ~5 comments) on EVERY thread open. The roots query (:1134) also embeds `{ replies: { some: VISIBLE_COMMENT } }`, an EXISTS on parentId with the same gap. Comment.deleteMany cascades and the author-side cascade (User delete → Comment.authorId, also unindexed) compound it.
findings.evidence: feed/actions.ts:1147-1152 quoted: `const rows = await prisma.comment.findMany({ where: { OR: [ { id: { in: rootIds }, ...VISIBLE_COMMENT }, { parentId: { in: rootIds }, ...VISIBLE_COMMENT } ] }, ...`. Schema Comment model lines 431-455 carry only the two postId-leading indexes; `parent Comment? @relation("CommentReplies", fields: [parentId], references: [id])` has no @@index([parentId]).
findings.fixDirection: Add `@@index([parentId])` to Comment (same manual-migration batch). Optionally also @@index([authorId]) for the export/purge/profile paths.
findings.gateOrTest: Same schema-assertion unit test; orchestrator EXPLAIN on the OR query shape (Bitmap/Index scan after adding the index).
findings.reproPlan: Read-only EXPLAIN of the quoted query shape with two dummy ids.

findings.title: Directory page ships every located member to the browser on every load and every filter change: the map pin query has no take and buildPins serializes each person once per listed city
findings.expected: The directory should stay usable at 2,000 members: bounded payloads, and per-interaction cost independent of total membership.
findings.actual: `prisma.user.findMany({ where: pinWhere, select: PIN_SELECT, orderBy: [...] })` (directory/page.tsx:294-298) has no `take` — it fetches every non-blocked member who has any UserPlace, with ~10 scalar fields plus their full places array. buildPins (:92-169) then pushes a full PinPerson object into `people` for EVERY resolvable city the member lists (`existing.people.push(person)` :160), so a member with 3 cities is serialized 3 times. The whole structure is passed as props to the client component `<DirectoryClient users cityPins unmappedPeople ...>` (:344-350), i.e. serialized into the RSC payload of every directory load. At 2,000 members with places this is on the order of 0.5-1.5MB of flight payload per view — on every filter change too, since filters navigate via searchParams and re-run the entire 7-query Promise.all (two full groupBys, a count, the pins, the city facet) server-side each time. Members on Indian mobile connections will feel this directly; it also multiplies function memory/CPU per request. (Below Stage 1 `people` is stripped (:333-335) but the query and buildPins still run.)
findings.evidence: directory/page.tsx:294-298 quoted: `prisma.user.findMany({ where: pinWhere, select: PIN_SELECT, orderBy: [{ batchYear: "desc" }, { name: "asc" }] })` — the only findMany in the Promise.all without take. PIN_SELECT (:42-57) includes `places: { select: { city: true, lat: true, lng: true }, orderBy: { position: "asc" } }`. :159-162: `existing.count += 1; existing.people.push(person)`.
findings.fixDirection: Cap what ships: send pins as {city, lng, lat, count} only and lazy-load a pin's people on drilldown via a server action (paginated), or cap people-per-pin (e.g. first 12 + count). Keep the aggregate count server-side. Also consider caching the unfiltered pin aggregation (it is identical for every viewer above Stage 1) with a short revalidate.
findings.gateOrTest: An e2e assertion on /directory response size (fail above e.g. 300KB), seeded with a few hundred members; or a unit test on buildPins output size bounds.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: load /directory with chrome-devtools MCP and read the document+RSC transfer size from list_network_requests; compare against member count.

findings.title: CommentLike has no commentId-leading index: per-comment like counts on every thread open scan the whole CommentLike table
findings.expected: `_count.commentLikes` per comment should be an index lookup on commentId.
findings.actual: CommentLike's only index is `@@unique([userId, commentId])` (userId-leading). loadComments includes `_count: { select: { commentLikes: true } }` (feed/actions.ts:1168) for every comment in the thread batch — a grouped count WHERE commentId IN (...) that cannot use the unique index and scans the table (plausible tens of thousands of rows at 2,000 users) on every thread open, stacking on the parentId scan from the sibling finding. The viewer's own-like lookup (`commentLikes: { where: { userId } }`, :1169 area) is fine via the unique.
findings.evidence: Schema: `model CommentLike { ...; @@unique([userId, commentId]) }` — no other index. feed/actions.ts:1168: `_count: { select: { commentLikes: true } }`.
findings.fixDirection: Add `@@index([commentId])` to CommentLike in the same manual migration batch.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only EXPLAIN of `SELECT "commentId", COUNT(*) FROM "CommentLike" WHERE "commentId" IN ('x') GROUP BY 1`.

findings.title: PollVote has no pollOptionId or postId index: poll vote counts scan PollVote on every feed page that contains a poll, and Post/PollOption deletion cascades scan it too
findings.expected: Vote counts per option (WHERE pollOptionId = ?) and the two FK cascades (pollOptionId, postId) should be indexed lookups.
findings.actual: PollVote's only index is `@@unique([userId, postId])`. The feed include `pollOptions: { orderBy: { position: "asc" }, include: { _count: { select: { votes: true } } } }` (feed/actions.ts:862-865) counts votes per option for every poll post on every feed page — unindexed on pollOptionId, so it scans the PollVote table. PollOption itself also has no postId index (schema:596-604), so loading options per post and the Post→PollOption cascade scan too (PollOption stays small, but it is the same class). Deleting a post with votes cascades on PollVote.postId — not leading in the unique either.
findings.evidence: Schema: `model PollVote { id ...; pollOptionId String; userId String; postId String; ... @@unique([userId, postId]) }` and `model PollOption { id ...; postId String; ... }` with no @@index blocks. feed/actions.ts:864: `include: { _count: { select: { votes: true } } }`.
findings.fixDirection: Add `@@index([pollOptionId])` and `@@index([postId])` to PollVote, and `@@index([postId])` to PollOption, in the same migration batch.

findings.title: PhotoLove has no photoId-leading index: Collection grid love-counts scan the PhotoLove table on every grid page, shuffle view, and photo detail
findings.expected: `_count.loves` per photo (WHERE photoId = ?) should be an index lookup.
findings.actual: PhotoLove's only index is `@@unique([userId, photoId])`. `includeFor` (collection/actions.ts:83-87) attaches `_count: { select: { loves: true } }` to every photo row in the grid (take 60 per page, :455/:478), the shuffle branch, and getMyPendingPhotos — each render is a grouped count WHERE photoId IN (...60) over an unindexed column, scanning the whole PhotoLove table (plausible 10-50k rows at 2,000 users). The Photo→PhotoLove delete cascade has the same gap.
findings.evidence: Schema: `model PhotoLove { id ...; userId String; photoId String; ... @@unique([userId, photoId]) }`. collection/actions.ts:83-87 quoted: `const includeFor = (userId: string) => ({ uploader: {...}, _count: { select: { loves: true } }, loves: { where: { userId }, select: { id: true } } })`.
findings.fixDirection: Add `@@index([photoId])` to PhotoLove in the same migration batch.

findings.title: Post has no authorId index: every profile view runs three-plus sequential scans of the Post table (two tab counts, the photo grid, the Posts tab), plus export and purge paths
findings.expected: Posts-by-author (WHERE authorId = ? ORDER BY createdAt DESC) is one of the hottest shapes (profile page) and should be served by a composite [authorId, createdAt] index. Postgres does not auto-index FKs.
findings.actual: Post's indexes are [groupId, createdAt], [kind, createdAt], [createdAt] — nothing leads with authorId. The profile page runs `post.count({ ...visiblePostsWhere, kind: "post" })`, `post.count({ ..., kind: "letter" })` (profile/[id]/page.tsx:144-148, where visiblePostsWhere = `{ authorId: user.id, isHidden: false, groupId: null, ... }` :130-139) and `post.findMany({ ...visiblePostsWhere, NOT: { images: null } }, orderBy createdAt desc, take 60)` (:151-155), and the Posts tab calls loadPosts({ authorId }) (feed/actions.ts:828). Each is a scan of the whole Post table (~20k rows plausible) filtered on an unindexed column, per profile view — profiles being a hot surface at 2,000 members. The account export (export/route.ts:87-91) and the User→Post cascade in purge share the gap. The [kind, createdAt] index helps none of them because kind is combined with authorId, not a substitute for it.
findings.evidence: schema.prisma:414-416 quoted: `@@index([groupId, createdAt]) @@index([kind, createdAt]) @@index([createdAt])` — the complete index list for Post. profile/[id]/page.tsx:130-131: `const visiblePostsWhere = { authorId: user.id, isHidden: false, groupId: null, ... }`.
findings.fixDirection: Add `@@index([authorId, createdAt])` to Post in the same migration batch.
findings.gateOrTest: Schema-assertion unit test; EXPLAIN on `SELECT count(*) FROM "Post" WHERE "authorId"='x' AND "kind"='post'`.

findings.title: Remaining unindexed FK columns make account purge and per-user lookups table-scans: CatchupEntryLove.entryId, Bookmark.postId, GroupMember.userId, Comment.authorId, Photo.uploaderId, CatchupEntry.authorId, CatchupPrompt.authorId
findings.expected: Every FK that is queried from the child side (counts, per-user lists, ON DELETE CASCADE) needs a child-side index; the purge transaction in particular must not degrade to a chain of sequential scans.
findings.actual: All of these uniques lead with the wrong column for their hot read: CatchupEntryLove `@@unique([userId, entryId])` — the round page counts loves per entry (`_count: { select: { loves: true } }`, round/[editionId]/page.tsx:275) and the archive teaser does too, both WHERE entryId; Bookmark `@@unique([userId, postId])` — the Post→Bookmark cascade scans on post delete; GroupMember `@@unique([groupId, userId])` — `groupMember.findMany({ where: { userId } })` runs on every saved-posts load (feed/actions.ts:955) and catchups home (catchups/page.tsx:65), userId not leading; Comment.authorId, Photo.uploaderId, CatchupEntry.authorId, CatchupPrompt.authorId have no index at all and are hit by the export route, photoQuotaError (`photo.count({ where: { uploaderId } })`, collection/actions.ts:96) and the User-delete cascade inside `prisma.$transaction([...])` (account-purge.ts:99). Individually these tables are smaller than Like/Comment, but the purge fires them all inside one transaction over a pgbouncer pooled connection: at 2,000-user table sizes a purge of an active member becomes a multi-second-to-minutes transaction, and the retention sweep runs purges in sequence (retention.ts:120-126) inside one cron invocation against Vercel's function duration ceiling.
findings.evidence: Schema quoted: CatchupEntryLove `@@unique([userId, entryId])` (no entryId index); GroupMember `@@unique([groupId, userId])`; Bookmark `@@unique([userId, postId])`; Comment/Photo/CatchupEntry/CatchupPrompt author/uploader columns have no @@index. account-purge.ts:99: `await prisma.$transaction([ prisma.report.deleteMany({ where: { reporterId: userId } }), <user.delete cascade> ])`.
findings.fixDirection: Same manual migration batch: @@index([entryId]) on CatchupEntryLove, @@index([postId]) on Bookmark, @@index([userId]) on GroupMember, @@index([authorId]) on Comment, @@index([uploaderId]) on Photo, @@index([authorId]) on CatchupEntry and CatchupPrompt. Cheap to write, and they close the purge-transaction risk in one stroke.
findings.gateOrTest: One schema-assertion unit test covering the full FK-index list pins all of these at once.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only EXPLAIN per shape; or time purgeUserAccount against a seeded throwaway user in dev (write — orchestrator's call, not mine).

findings.title: Catchup home archive is an unbounded N+1 that fetches every answer body ever written: one query per published Round, sequentially, each pulling full entry bodies to build a 140-char teaser
findings.expected: The archive strip should cost O(1) queries and fetch only what it renders (a count and a 140-char teaser per Round).
findings.actual: `publishedEditions` is fetched with no take (:368-372), then a for loop (:375-379) awaits `prisma.catchupEntry.findMany({ where: { editionId: ed.id }, select: { authorId: true, body: true, _count: { select: { loves: true } } } })` once PER edition — sequential round trips that grow forever with the Catch-up's life (a monthly group in year 3 pays ~36 sequential queries per home view), each dragging every entry's FULL body across the wire to compute `contributorCount` and slice 140 chars (:380-388). The `_count.loves` inside it hits the unindexed CatchupEntryLove.entryId per batch. The catchups index page repeats the over-fetch pattern at page.tsx:211: `entries: { select: { authorId: true, body: true, _count: { select: { loves: true } } } }` — all entries with full bodies for 6 editions on every /catchups load.
findings.evidence: Quoted from [catchupId]/page.tsx:374-379: `const archive: HomeArchiveRow[] = []; for (const ed of publishedEditions) { const entries = await prisma.catchupEntry.findMany({ where: { editionId: ed.id }, select: { authorId: true, body: true, _count: { select: { loves: true } } } });` — findMany at :368 has select {id, number, publishedAt} and no take.
findings.fixDirection: Replace the loop with one query: `catchupEntry.findMany({ where: { editionId: { in: ids } }, select: { editionId, authorId, ... } })` grouped in JS, or two groupBys (contributors per edition, top-loved entry per edition); truncate body in SQL (substring) or fetch only the top-loved entry's body per edition. Cap the archive list (take 24) with a 'Show older' path.
findings.gateOrTest: A unit test on the archive loader asserting query count is constant regardless of edition count (Prisma query-event counter), or at minimum a take on publishedEditions.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: open a catchup home with several published rounds and count queries via Prisma log locally.

findings.title: Seven fire-and-forget telemetry writes (recordView x4, logSearch x3) run without after(): on Vercel the write races response completion and is silently dropped, so view counters and search logs undercount in production only
findings.expected: On serverless, nothing is guaranteed to run after the response unless scheduled with after()/waitUntil. The codebase knows this — the mail drain (layout.tsx:63) and the collection intake (feed/actions.ts:180) both use after() — and the ContentView/SearchLog tables exist specifically to answer the owner's analytics questions.
findings.actual: All seven sites fire the promise bare: `void recordView(session.user.id, "profile", user.id)` (profile/[id]/page.tsx:117, with the comment 'Not awaited: a profile must render at the same speed...'), same shape in letters/[id]:85, collection/[id]:58, round/[editionId]:194, and `void logSearch({...})` in users/search:72, places/search:127, feed/page.tsx:31. When the RSC render or route response finishes before the DB round trip does, Vercel freezes the instance and the write is lost. The loss is probabilistic (fast DB round trips sometimes win the race), so the symptom is production counters that are mysteriously lower than dev — exactly the failure class CLAUDE.md's own guard-that-hides-its-breakage note warns about, and invisible because both helpers swallow errors in production (content-view.ts:34-38, search-log.ts:80-84).
findings.evidence: profile/[id]/page.tsx:114-117 quoted: `/* Not awaited: ... */ void recordView(session.user.id, "profile", user.id);`. Contrast layout.tsx:63: `after(async () => { await drainMailQueue(); ... })` — the pattern exists in the same tree and is not used here.
findings.fixDirection: Wrap each call in next/server after(): `after(() => recordView(...))` in the four pages, and in the two route handlers plus the feed page use after() as well (route handlers support it). No behavior change for the member; the write is guaranteed to complete post-response.
findings.gateOrTest: Grep-gate in the unit tests: fail on `void recordView(` / `void logSearch(` outside an after() callback; or simply verify ContentView rows increment on the deployed site after a profile visit.
findings.reproPlan: Live proof on production is read-write telemetry; safer code-argument-only. Orchestrator could compare ContentView.count deltas against PostHog pageview counts for the same period (read-only).

findings.title: SearchLog's keystroke dedupe does not do what its comment guarantees: each prefix of a typed query is a distinct string, so type-ahead writes a row (plus a dedupe read) per keystroke, into a table the retention sweep never prunes
findings.expected: Per the in-file comment (search-log.ts:22-29): 'typing "Bengaluru" would otherwise write nine rows, of which eight are prefixes nobody searched for. Debouncing in the browser helps but cannot be trusted, so the dedupe lives here where it is guaranteed.' The table should grow with searches, not keystrokes, and old rows should age out.
findings.actual: The implemented dedupe (search-log.ts:50-58) matches on EXACT query equality: `where: { userId, scope, query, createdAt: { gte: ... } }`. 'Ben' ≠ 'Beng' ≠ 'Benga', so every keystroke of a type-ahead surface (users/search and places/search both call logSearch per request, and both back per-keystroke pickers — the 'search' rate limit comment at rate-limit.ts:88 says 'one request per keystroke') still writes its own row, exactly the nine-rows-for-Bengaluru case the comment claims is prevented. Each miss also costs an extra findFirst before the create. Compounding it: runRetentionSweep (retention.ts:74-110) prunes AdminMessage, Report, Contribution, Notification, LoginAttempt, AuditLog and OutboundEmail — but neither SearchLog nor Visit appears in KEEP_DAYS, so both grow without bound on a 500MB-class Supabase plan (SearchLog at keystroke rate; Visit at ~one row per member-sitting). The 'most common searches' analytics is also polluted by prefix fragments.
findings.evidence: search-log.ts:50-55 quoted: `const recent = await prisma.searchLog.findFirst({ where: { userId: input.userId, scope: input.scope, query, createdAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now() - DEDUPE_MS) } } ...)` — `query` is the exact trimmed string (:45). retention.ts KEEP_DAYS block lists seven tables; SearchLog and Visit are absent from both KEEP_DAYS and the sweep steps.
findings.fixDirection: Two independent fixes: (1) make the dedupe prefix-aware — before insert, delete (or update-in-place) a recent row from the same user+scope whose query is a PREFIX of the new one (`WHERE query = left(:new, length(query))` via startsWith), or debounce server-side by keying on (userId, scope) within the window and keeping only the longest query; (2) add SearchLog (e.g. 365 days) and Visit (e.g. 365 days) to KEEP_DAYS and the sweep.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on logSearch: log 'Be' then 'Ben' then 'Beng' within a second and assert one surviving row; a retention test asserting the sweep deletes old SearchLog/Visit rows.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: count SearchLog rows grouped by user+minute on the live DB and observe prefix chains ('Be','Ben','Beng' with ascending createdAt).

findings.title: Resend launch math, quantified: 95/day cap minus the 20-message reset reserve leaves 75 verification emails per day, so 400 day-one signups means the last member waits 5-6 days for their link — locked below Stage 1 (no directory names, no profiles) the entire time
findings.expected: The owner accepted queuing beyond 100/day (OutboundEmail model comment: 'Launch is expected to put more than 100 signups through in the first day... The rest wait for tomorrow'). What has not been surfaced is the compounding tail: 'tomorrow' is only true for the first 75 in line.
findings.actual: DAILY_CAP = 95 (email-queue.ts:80), RESET_RESERVE = 20 (:91), and the drain's eligibility filter (:468-469: `live.verifyRemaining > 0 ? ["verify", "reset", "password-changed"] : ["reset", "password-changed"]`) means at most 75 verify messages leave per UTC day. Queue math for the owner's own launch estimate: 400 signups day one → day 1 sends 75, backlog 325; day 2: 250; day 3: 175; day 4: 100; day 5: 25; day 6: clear — before counting days 2-5's NEW signups, which join the same FIFO behind them. Every waiting member is meanwhile held below Stage 1: requireVerifiedEmail gates the directory names, profile pages, people search and users-by-batch (directory/page.tsx:196 `namesLocked = !IS_DEMO && !session?.user?.emailConfirmed`; users/search/route.ts:18), so the first-week experience for most of the launch cohort is a browsable shell with no people in it, with the banner honestly reporting the budget is spent (verificationMailState 'queued'). The queue mechanics themselves are sound (claim CAS, token minted at send, reserve protects resets) — the finding is the number.
findings.evidence: email-queue.ts:80 `const DAILY_CAP = 95;`, :91 `const RESET_RESERVE = 20;`, :461-476 the BATCH loop with `eligibleKinds`. schema.prisma OutboundEmail header comment: 'Launch is expected to put more than 100 signups through in the first day (owner, 2026-08-11)'.
findings.fixDirection: A launch-week decision, not code: either pay for one month of Resend's first paid tier (raises the daily cap ~50x; DAILY_CAP could then read from env), or pre-verify the roster-matched cohort (RosterEntry emails whose signup address matches could skip the mail gate), or temporarily relax which surfaces Stage 1 gates during launch week. Any of the three collapses the 6-day tail; the code needs only DAILY_CAP to become configurable.
findings.gateOrTest: A unit test pinning verifyRemaining = DAILY_CAP - RESET_RESERVE so a future edit to either constant is a conscious act; an admin/mail banner already shows sentToday/dailyCap.

findings.title: Two admin lists are unbounded and grow forever: /admin/support fetches every Contribution row ever recorded, /admin/reports fetches every pending report, both with joins
findings.expected: Admin lists should be paginated or capped like their siblings (admin/mail takes 50/50/20, admin/audit takes 100, admin people is keyset-paginated).
findings.actual: admin/support/page.tsx:59-71: `prisma.contribution.findMany({ select: { id, amount, status, livemode, method, failureReason, createdAt, paidAt, user: { select: { id, name } } }, orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" } })` — no take; Contribution is retained 10 years (retention.ts KEEP_DAYS.contributions = 3650) and includes every abandoned checkout row ('created' rows are normal per the model comment), so this list grows monotonically for a decade. admin/reports/page.tsx:45-49 fetches all pending reports with REPORT_SELECT joins and no take (the resolved list below it does take 50). Admin-only blast radius, but at 2,000 users over years these pages get slower every month with no ceiling.
findings.evidence: Quoted above; contrast the same file's sibling query at reports/page.tsx:50-55 which has `take: 50`.
findings.fixDirection: Add take (e.g. 200) plus a count header, or reuse the keyset pattern from admin-people-query.ts. For support, also consider aggregating totals in SQL (sum/groupBy already exist in admin-analytics.ts) instead of shipping every row.
findings.gateOrTest: Lint-style unit test asserting every admin page findMany carries take, or just the page-level take.

findings.title: Production images are served from pub-*.r2.dev, which Cloudflare rate-limits and documents as not for production; mostly shielded by the Vercel image optimizer's cache, but unoptimized call sites and first-fetches bypass the shield
findings.expected: At 2,000 users, image-heavy surfaces (feed, collection) need an origin that is not rate-limited. Cloudflare's docs state r2.dev URLs are rate-limited and intended for development; the custom-domain step is acknowledged in AGENTS.md ('a custom domain can be added before launch') but is not on the bugs.md open list and has no tracking item.
findings.actual: next.config.ts:166-172 allows `hostname: "*.r2.dev"` and the comment confirms serving from pub-<hash>.r2.dev today. Most member traffic goes through /_next/image, whose edge cache absorbs repeats — but every cache-miss (each new image x each device size), every `unoptimized` <Image> (conversation.tsx:112, message-composer.tsx:152 render admin-thread screenshots straight from the r2.dev URL), and any OG/scraper fetch hits r2.dev directly. Under launch-day load Cloudflare may throttle (429/slow) with no error surfaced anywhere — images just intermittently fail. Severity Low because the optimizer covers the hot paths; it becomes Medium the day a burst of new uploads meets a burst of viewers.
findings.evidence: next.config.ts:167 comment quoted: '// Cloudflare R2 (pub-<hash>.r2.dev now; a custom domain can be added later).' conversation.tsx:112: `unoptimized`.
findings.fixDirection: Before launch: attach the R2 bucket to a custom domain (owner dashboard action — pairs with the CORS/admin-token item already in memory), update R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL and the remotePattern. Until then, remove `unoptimized` from the two message components so even screenshots ride the optimizer cache.
findings.gateOrTest: A unit test asserting R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is not *.r2.dev when VERCEL_ENV=production (env-shape check), added once the domain exists.
findings.reproPlan: Orchestrator: read-only curl of a pub-*.r2.dev object in a loop to observe Cloudflare throttling headers — or accept Cloudflare's documentation as the evidence.

6i-concurrency on the shared jobs this lens touched: mail drain claim is a CAS updateMany (email-queue.ts:160-164) and the 95-vs-100 slack absorbs the budget read race; catchup advance uses CAS + re-read (catchups.ts:869-880) and openNextRound CASes nextOpensAt inside a transaction with the [catchupId, number] unique as backstop (:917-938); Visit writes are single upserts on a proxy-minted PK with a derived (not random) cold-start fallback (proxy.ts:267-291) — the historical duplicate-visit race is genuinely closed.

6f-third-party quotas quantified CLEAN at 2,000 users: Upstash — 24 limiter call sites, all on writes/auth/type-ahead, zero per-pageview calls; realistic day ≈ 300 logins x2 getRemaining + ~1.5k type-ahead keystrokes + ~500 write checks < 3k commands vs the 10k/day free tier (worst launch day ~4-5k) — fail-open never triggers from quota at this scale. Sentry 5k errors/mo: server-only SDK, deploy-only enablement — fine. Turnstile (signup/login/forgot only) and PostHog (~180k events/mo at realistic engagement vs 1M free) — fine. R2 storage/ops bounded by the per-account photo quota.

6g-R2 key throttling (1 write/sec/key): every upload key is uploads/<userId>/<year>/<month>/<cuid>.webp — cuid filenames, so no key is ever written twice; presign mints a fresh key per request (storage.ts:50-55, 96-107, 155-165). Clean.
